recipes.name: Apple and Brown Sugar Corned Beef
ingredients_raw: 2 (3 pound) corned beef briskets with spice packets
1 head cabbage, cored and cut into large chunks

steps.text: Pour apple juice into a large slow cooker. Mix in brown sugar and mustard, stirring until brown sugar has dissolved. Mix in the contents of the spice packets, then lay briskets into apple juice mixture. Top with potatoes, cabbage chunks, onions, and carrots, then push vegetables into liquid.
Cover and cook on High for 4 to 5 hours or on Low for 8 to 10 hours, until corned beef is very tender. Slice the meat thinly across the grain and serve with the vegetables.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple and Brown Sugar Corned Beef
raw_recipe.description: This brown sugar corned beef features brisket, potatoes, carrots, and cabbage simmered in a slow cooker with apple juice, brown sugar, and mustard.

review.reviewBody:
MY dad of all people started making this and it wasn't MY traditional way. I gave him "the eye" while watching him throw apple juice and mustard of all things into it. I must admit..."the eye" felt stupid as I was eating the most delicious corn beef dinner EVER! The cabbage was almost like a dessert. I couldn't stop eating. Don't mess with this recipe other than maybe trying it out in a pressure cooker. But doubt it even needs that!
Ambra-Akron

Asian cooking tells us to balance the salt, sweet, bitter, umami. Finally, this recipe reminds us of these principles. It is the correct recipe for this salty meat because it's all about balance. Rinse the meat before cooking. I used a 2.2 lb brisket and cooked it on the stove in 4 c water, 1 c unsweetened apple sauce, 1/2 c molasses, and a fat 1/4 c yellow mustard with the spice packet and black pepper. It cooked in three hours. I then pulled the meat for slicing and cooked small potatoes, carrots, onions, and Cabbage until tender in the fat skimmed braising liquid. Delicious and not sweet. The flavors were balanced.

I made this using the stove top method. We really enjoyed it. My husband couldn't stop raving. I made a few changes I only added carrots and onions (though next time I make it I will add potatoes ) and because it was Passover I couldn't use mustard. The corned beef I used did not come with a spice pack. It was still delish. One hint: I rewarmed the meat and veggies in the oven before serving and the meat turned a brown and the sauce thickened.A 5 star + recipe.Thanks for sharing
No changes except to reduce the apple juice and add 4 ounces of a dark stout. Putting the corned beef in the oven to caramelize and finish is the best idea ever. Will definitely do again.

This recipe will be my go-to recipe for corned beef. Used it with small briskets…flat cut and point cut. Both were super delicious and tender. The cut that chunks vs the cut that slices seemed to be more flavorful. Added some celery pieces. Cooked 9 hours in my slow cooker, removed to platter and covered in foil for 15 minutes before serving.

This is AMAZING! My family loved it. Only changes I cut back a little on juice and sugar after reading some reviews re desert etc. Added I cup of low salt beef broth to compensate for liquid doubled the carrots Yum. I made on stove top it was not too sweet and next time will add full sweetness as original recipe calls for. This recipe is dead on delish!!! Found my go to corned beef recipe for life! Enjoy and Thank U so much for this awesome recipe! :)
Add the veggies the last hour. 1/2 is not enough time for the potatoes to cook.

It was delicious. I cut back the brown sugar to a scant 1/3 C.
I made 6# of beef thinking there would be plenty for left overs.

They licked the platter clean! There were only 4 of us.

I used apple cider, and a little more mustard and brown sugar. I transferred the carrots and potatoes to a baking sheet to roast them a bit in the oven, and added the cabbage to the cooker at this time just until the cabbage was wilted. I made this once before and my son's loved it, so we are having it again tonight!

This was my third and final attempt at finding a corn beef and cabbage recipe that we liked. This was great! My brisket was a little less than three pounds so I only used half of the ingredients all except the brown sugar, instead of using half, a quarter cup, I used one packed tablespoon and that was perfect. The next time I make it , I will probably leave the brown sugar out.

This recipe was awesome. The only thing I changed and I'm glad I did was to cook the potatoes by themselves. I don't think I would have liked my potatoes that sweet. The next time I will cook the cabbage and potatoes together and just add the carrots to the meat. The cabbage was a little too sweet for me. Otherwise a great recipe that I will certainly do again.
I made this for a group of men at an event that happened to fall on St. Patrick's Day. They loved it, and so did I. I made it exactly as written.
My go to recipe now.
Made it several times. Family loves it!11
This is the only recipe that I’ve found where I actually enjoy eating corned beef! Thanks for this one, it’s definitely a favorite for ☘️ St. Patrick’s Day!!
Delicious! I didn't change a thing. We were concerned that it would be too sweet, but it wasn't.

This method is A+ for sure. I used apple cider rather than apple juice, but otherwise stuck to the recipe... mostly, as my slow cooker didn't have as much space for potatoes as OP's. I opted for the low and slow setting. It came out perfect. I've tried corned beef so many different ways over the years. And this has been my absolute favorite. I ended up having to repeat the process with another the next day, as my family devoured the whole thing before I even had a chance to glance at the tupperware. So, if you're like me, and don't have a huge crockpot, plan ahead if you want any left-overs at all.
Turned out great. Cut the recipe down to fit my brisket. And left the cabbage out. Couldn’t bring myself to ruin a good chunk of meat.

I made this recipe last night and it was absolutely delicious! the corned beef and veggies came out so flavorful and perfectly tender! I added some froz carrots I had the last 1/2 hr and it was perfect! will make this again and again...
I make this every year and it is one of the culinary highlights of the year. The recipe needs no alterations and the corned beef hash the next morning is just as wonderful
